priority.description:
The priority for invalidation queue entries generated by the job.  When null, the priority will be that specified
in @invalidationQueueOptions(priority).  This field will be modified by the setPriority function to override the
default.  Avoid setting manually as that will not update the priority of already submitted invalidations.

disabled.description:
Indicates that the job is in the disabled state meaning that no queue entries will be processed for the job.
This should only be set manually when initially creating/starting the job.  To disable/enable a running job call
{@link disable}/{@link enable}.

maxConcurrency.description:
The maximum number of invalidation queue entries that will be processed simultaneously for a job.  If -1, no limit
is applied. This is enforced independently of {@link maxConcurrencyPerNode}.

maxConcurrencyPerNode.description:
The maximum number of invalidation queue entries that will be processed simultaneously for a job per node.  If -1,
no limit is applied.  This is enforced independently of {@link maxConcurrency}.

runAsUser.description:
{@see TestRunner.runAsUser}

Must be set to true for calls to {@link TestRunner.testPackage}.

nodePool.description:
When non-null, invalidation queue entries for the job will only be processed by servers with a matching
nodePool.  When null, invalidation queue entries for the job will only be processed by servers from default
nodePool.

skipIfRunning.description:
If true, attempts to start the job will be ignored if it is already running and no error will be thrown.  This is useful,
for instance, if a cron job starts a job and the job from a previous cron invocation may not have completed before the next
scheduled run.

If false, an error will be thrown if an attempt is made to start the job if it is already running.

numAutoRecoveryAttempts.description: Set to between 1 and 5 to enable auto recovery. See {@link invalidation-queues.c3doc Invalidation Queues} for detailed documentation.

propagateActionContext.description:
If true, the job will propagate {@link Action.Context}.
This should only be set manually when starting the job.

excludedTests.description: Tests that should *not* be run when executing {@link TestRunner.testPackage}.

includePatterns.description:
Optional array of regexes to filter Jasmine `it` and `describe` blocks to only those that match one
or more of the patterns.

excludeCategories.description:
If this field is set, test all categories except for these.
Uncategorized tests will not be excluded
{@see TestCategory}
To exclude uncategorized tests, use the following TestRunnerConfig:
`TestRunnerConfig.make({includeCategories: TestCategory.values()})`

To exclude a test category, for instance, "performance", and uncategorized tests, use:
`TestRunnerConfig.make({includeCategories: TestCategory.values().filter((name) => name !== 'performance' )})`

actionMockBehavior.description: For ActionMocks, define the special behavior to use, if any.

noDependency.description: Test current package only or test all dependent packages

pkgName.description: The package for which the test is being run.

codeCoverage.description: The categories of code coverage to run. See {@link ActionLanguage} for possible languages, or pass "ALL" for all.

batchSize.description: The batch size to use. If a package has more than this number of tests, it will be split into multiple batches.

createBatchTags.description:
If true, each {@link TestRunner.processBatch} call will deploy a new tag and run the tests from the batch
within that new test tag. The tag id will be a unique string generated from the batch id.

If {@link batchSize} is set such that the tests will be run in multiple batches, this should likely be
set to true, so that tests in different batches running simultaneously do not interfere with each other.

createBatchUsers.description:
If true, each {@link TestRunner.processBatch} call will create a new {@link User}, grant it privileges
based on the permissions of the user who started the job, and run the tests from the batch
as that new user.

If {@link batchSize} is set such that the tests will be run in multiple batches, and some of the tests
impersonate other users, this should likely be set to true, so that tests in different batches running
simultaneously do not interfere with each other.

stopOnFailure.description:
If true, tests will stop all execution on the first thrown error or failed expectation, instead of continuing
to process subsequent suites and specs and reporting all failures at the end.

instrumentedCode.description:
Instrumented code generated by TestRunner that should be used instead of deployed application logic code.
Key is file URL. Value is the instrumented JS/Python/R code.

uninstrumentedCode.description:
Original code to redeploy after running with code coverage.
Key is file URL. Value is the uninstrumented JS/Python/R code.

tagDeployTests.description:
Tests that require a full redeploy before re-running because they are not
idempotent (usually because they modify metadata and resetting the metadata
is too expensive when they do not fail).

title: Configuration object optionally passed to {@link TestRunner.testPackage} to indicate how to start the job.
name: TestRunnerConfig
